Fixed in shipped CPython3.12.16 security release despite CPE fix-version metadata listing only3.14.0. Its Lib/mimetypes.py explicitly sets knownfiles=[] on win32; it does not read user-writable Unix-style MIME locations.

Alternate Base64 spellings do not bypass CivicCast authorization: subscription HMAC verifies the decoded bytes, AES-GCM authenticates the decoded envelope, and paywall signatures verify canonical parsed payload bytes. They do not authorize by the textual Base64 spelling or forward it to a different decoder. Installer/signature inputs use validate=True. The upstream change is an alphabet-deprecation warning, not a cryptographic fix.

No cross-decoder authorization boundary: subscription/AES-GCM/paywall authenticate the decoded payload itself. Untrusted signed-package, federation and recovery inputs use validate=True. Other permissive calls consume locally generated worker commands, stored salts, or already-validated timestamp proofs, not a second interpretation of attacker-controlled trailing data.
The vulnerable IMAP command API is not used by CivicCast: no product import or call of imaplib; mail delivery uses SMTP. No user-controlled IMAP command reaches the shipped standard-library function.

getaddrinfo() truncating a host at an embedded null byte cannot bypass a CivicCast outbound-destination check: every guard over untrusted hosts (ActivityPub remote fetch, CG feed fetcher, subscription webhooks) decides by RESOLVING the name with getaddrinfo and rejecting non-global resulting addresses, and the connection resolves through the same function (ActivityPub and webhooks additionally pin the validated address), so check and connect see the same truncated name. No product check allow-lists by host-name string before resolution; the trusted-host set in subscribe/router.py resolves only this machine's own hostname. Upstream fix is in 3.16.0; revisit when a 3.12 security release carries it.
The vulnerable POP command API is not used by CivicCast: no product import or call of poplib; mail delivery uses SMTP. No user-controlled POP command reaches the shipped standard-library function.
CivicCast never calls http.cookies.Morsel.js_output. Cookies are HTTP response headers, not this inline script generator; no route embeds a cookie value through the vulnerable API.

Upstream disputes this as a vulnerability: pkgutil.get_data follows the same trust model as open. CivicCast does not use it to resolve user-provided resource paths. No product call to pkgutil.get_data exists.

CPython3.12.16 includes the tempfile cleanup hardening (gh157579); Windows rmtree still has an upstream residual race if an attacker can modify the temporary tree. Native service temporary work runs as the installed service account in its private temporary directories; input files are copied/parsed, not arbitrary filesystem mutation authority. Provisioning state is explicitly ACL-restricted. Same-account/admin filesystem compromise is not prevented by this assessment. No claim that Windows rmtree is universally symlink-safe.

The shipped closure contains libintl-9.dll message-catalog runtime, not GNU msgfmt/PO catalog compiler. Vulnerable default_add_message/read-catalog.c and po_gram_parse are compiler code and not reachable via this runtime DLL. The PostgreSQL pack explicitly selects runtime binaries and excludes msgfmt.

Finding requires an untrusted FreeType face lifecycle (reported via Poppler PDF rendering). GStreamer closure does not ship Poppler; original-PDF rendering/OCR uses PDFium. Product graphics use its built-in bitmap font and no uploaded font API; any Pango font selection uses installed system fonts. No attacker-provided PDF/font reaches Cairo FreeType font teardown in this product. This is a product-applicability assessment, not an upstream fix.

The vulnerability requires XML_ParserReset reuse of one native parser. Pinned CPython pyexpat.c and _elementtree.c neither call nor expose XML_ParserReset; each parser is created with XML_ParserCreate_MM. Stdlib SAX reset constructs another ParserCreate object. Actual shipped3.12.16/Expat2.9.0 exposes no Reset method. This is API non-reachability, not a claim that Expat2.9.0 fixes the issue.

Supported untrusted CAP/RSS XML parsing uses existing defusedxml with forbid_dtd=True and forbid_entities=True, aborting at the DTD declaration before entity amplification. Regression tests cover a DTD beyond4096leadingbytes, and actual shipped3.12.16/Expat2.9.0 rejected both payloads. vMix already uses defusedxml entity rejection; remaining stdlib ET parse sites process internally generated exports/local validator reports, not raw feed XML. The underlying Expat2.9.0 library remains vulnerable for arbitrary callers who opt into parsing untrusted DTDs.

CPE range false positive against the exact shipped 3.8.1 source. The upstream fix bounds soup_headers_parse to positive lengths at most MAX_HEADERS_BUFFER_SIZE (256 KiB); the private header defines that bound. This is upstream issue 512 fix, not a claim that the parser ABI changed.

CPE range false positive against the exact shipped 3.8.1 source. The later Range regression is fixed: suffix lengths exceeding the resource are clamped to start zero; ERANGE is handled before addition. Upstream explicitly closes issue 516.

CPE range false positive against the exact shipped 3.8.1 source. URL-decoded hostnames are validated character by character (with explicit IP and IDNA handling) before accepting the URI, preventing CRLF in the proxy Host value.

CPE range false positive against the exact shipped 3.8.1 source. Content-Disposition uses set_content_foo, whose final replacement is SOUP_HEADER_VALUE_UNTRUSTED; the common append rejects CR or LF. Filename sanitization is also present.

CPE range false positive against the exact shipped 3.8.1 source. Cross-origin redirect handling explicitly removes Proxy-Authorization as well as Authorization; later auth-manager cached-proxy origin scoping is retained.

CPE range false positive against the exact shipped 3.8.1 source. Duplicate Content-Length values must parse without overflow/trailing junk and be byte-identical; conflicting values are rejected. The later identical-duplicate allowance preserves this protection.

CPE range false positive against the exact shipped 3.8.1 source. Server Digest auth tracks issued nonces with expiry and maximum nonce count under a mutex; unknown/expired/replayed counts are rejected and successful counts advance.

CPE range false positive against the exact shipped 3.8.1 source. Client URI hostnames pass strict is_host_valid validation; server Host values additionally reject controls, whitespace, percent encoding and URI delimiters before URI construction. CPE range false positive against the exact shipped 3.8.1 source. HTTP methods must conform to RFC 9110 token syntax; constructors and method setter call method_is_valid, rejecting CRLF.

CPE range false positive against the exact shipped 3.8.1 source. Content-Type uses set_content_foo with SOUP_HEADER_VALUE_UNTRUSTED, reaching the common CR/LF rejection rather than bypassing validation.

CPE range false positive against the exact shipped 3.8.1 source. The server HTTP/2 message I/O protects the nghttp2 session across reads/writes and defers destruction while protected; upstream explicitly closes issue 496.

CPE range false positive against the exact shipped 3.8.1 source. Cookie insertion is gated by allow_cookies_for_request, excluding HTTPS proxy CONNECT requests. The 3.8.1 follow-up releases the acquired connection reference without removing the gate.

CPE range false positive against the exact shipped 3.8.1 source. Boundary scanning is skipped when buffered bytes are shorter than the boundary, preventing unsigned subtraction underflow and client multipart over-read.

CPE range false positive against the exact shipped 3.8.1 source. Chunk size requires a leading hex digit and rejects trailing non-hex data; whitespace, plus prefixes and malformed suffixes no longer pass the numeric parser.

CPE range false positive against the exact shipped 3.8.1 source. Proxy authentication is skipped for an established CONNECT tunnel and any Proxy-Authorization request header is cleared before sending to the origin.

The original CPython 3.12.16 http.client parser is affected. CivicCast applies only upstream commit 2eb2af805c156ca52b316bb4ced5e0ab3971d0ae's Content-Length/chunk-size correction to the exact 3.12.16 source when assembling the app runtime. The original interpreter archive and independent provenance are verified before patching; installed verification requires the corrected stdlib ZIP SHA256 65551fbece52b878bf1bc9187b8bb4d2518767de4d3a4f9a6a64d4a79016681b and size 9030959. Every other stdlib member, native binary and PSF license remains unchanged. An isolated actual cached 3.12.16 interpreter proved the original accepted malformed framing, the backport rejects malformed chunks/ignores invalid Content-Length, and valid framing still works. The CPE-only version match does not recognize this pinned backport; this is not an exception for unpatched 3.12.16.

CVE-2019-16294 is Notepad++'s SciLexer.dll .ml lexer. pywin32 ships pythonwin/scintilla.dll only for its Pythonwin IDE, loaded through win32ui; CivicCast never imports win32ui or pythonwin and never opens files in a Scintilla editor. Reachable only if someone launches Pythonwin by hand.

The IMF demuxer IS compiled into this BtbN build and the upstream fix (FFmpeg pull 25341) is not merged as of 2026-11-06, so this rests on CivicCast never handing it an IMF package. The demuxer only reads a composition playlist that libxml2 parses as an XML document. civiccast.schedule.ingest.run_ffprobe, the single intake probe for staff uploads, file replacements, the watch folder and contributor submissions, refuses any file that begins as an XML document (every libxml2-autodetected encoding) before ffprobe runs; the refusal (UnsafeMediaError) is not an FfprobeError, so the contributor broken-media override cannot ingest past it. Residual, stated plainly: an operator-configured SRT/HLS/MPEG-TS network live source whose remote sender serves an IMF playlist would still be auto-detected; those endpoints are staff-configured (SRT passphrase-protected). Short review date: re-pin FFmpeg to a build with the upstream fix.
